newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa and Namibia sign debt relief agreement.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa and Namibia sign debt relief agreement.

text.p: Namibia and South Africa on Monday signed an agreement that Namibia would not have to repay 1.24 billion rand lent to it by South Africa during the apartheid era.
Finance Ministers Trevor Manuel and Nangolo Mbumba told reporters that the agreement marked the beginning of a new relationship between the two countries.

The debt was incurred before Namibia's independence in 1990 and consisted mainly of privately placed and domestic registered bonds held by South African financial institutions, as well as some foreign loans.

The South African parliament recently amended the Exchequer Act to allow for the writing off of the debt and Manuel and Mbumba will now ask their parliaments to officially ratify the agreement signed on Monday.
The agreement will come into force 30 days after ratification.
Manuel said the 1.24 billion rand was "one third of one percent of South Africa's debt as it stands now. It will merely be factored into what exists and will be redeemed over a period of time."
But for Namibia, the debt was considerable, Mbumba said, and its removal would provide his country with a solid basis from which to finance much needed development projects.
